title: Mongol siege and capture of Baghdad
summary: In early 1258 the Mongol army under Hulagu Khan attacked Baghdad, seat of the Abbasid caliph al-Mustasim. One encyclopedia dates the defeat of the caliph's army to 17 January and the surrender to 10 February; the caliph was put to death about ten days later, probably rolled in a carpet and trampled. Another account says the city was levelled and its population massacred. The Mongols thereby conquered the Abbasid Caliphate.

uncertainty.note: Both opened pages give 1258. Encyclopedia.com gives 17 January for the caliph's army defeat, the 22nd for Hulagu reaching the walls and 10 February for the surrender; World History Encyclopedia gives only the year. Exact dates and the caliph's death are not settled across accounts.

as_recorded.value: army defeated Jan. 17, 1258; surrender February 10; caliph put to death 10 days later

where.historical_name: Baghdad, capital of the Abbasid Caliphate

importance.justification: The Mongol conquest of Baghdad ended the Abbasid Caliphate in its capital.

audience_note: Describes the massacre of a city's population, the levelling of Baghdad and the execution of the caliph.
reviewer_note: Least sure of the exact days (the army defeat, surrender and caliph's death are given only by Encyclopedia.com) and the manner of the caliph's death, which the page calls only probable. No casualty figure is stated because the two pages opened give none.
